import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

def run(inputs: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]:
    customer_profile = inputs["customer_profile"].copy()
    profile_changes = inputs["profile_changes"].copy()
    
    # Handle empty inputs
    if profile_changes.empty:
        return {"new_profile": customer_profile[["customer_id", "email", "phone", "tier", "updated_seq"]].copy()}
    
    # Ensure proper types
    customer_profile["customer_id"] = customer_profile["customer_id"].astype("int64")
    customer_profile["updated_seq"] = customer_profile["updated_seq"].astype("int64")
    profile_changes["customer_id"] = profile_changes["customer_id"].astype("int64")
    profile_changes["change_seq"] = profile_changes["change_seq"].astype("int64")
    
    # Normalize email: LOWER(TRIM(email)) if not NULL and not the sentinel
    def normalize_email(val):
        if pd.isna(val) or val == "<<NULL>>":
            return val
        return str(val).strip().lower()
    
    profile_changes["email"] = profile_changes["email"].apply(normalize_email)
    customer_profile["email"] = customer_profile["email"].apply(normalize_email)
    
    # Build result by processing each customer
    result_rows = []
    
    # Get unique customer IDs from both tables
    all_customer_ids = set(customer_profile["customer_id"].unique())
    all_customer_ids.update(profile_changes["customer_id"].unique())
    
    for cust_id in sorted(all_customer_ids):
        # Get current profile state
        profile_rows = customer_profile[customer_profile["customer_id"] == cust_id]
        
        if len(profile_rows) > 0:
            # Customer exists
            current_email = profile_rows.iloc[0]["email"]
            current_phone = profile_rows.iloc[0]["phone"]
            current_tier = profile_rows.iloc[0]["tier"]
            current_seq = profile_rows.iloc[0]["updated_seq"]
            customer_exists = True
        else:
            # Customer does not exist yet
            current_email = np.nan
            current_phone = np.nan
            current_tier = np.nan
            current_seq = -1
            customer_exists = False
        
        # Get applicable changes
        changes = profile_changes[profile_changes["customer_id"] == cust_id].copy()
        
        if customer_exists:
            # Filter out changes with change_seq <= updated_seq
            changes = changes[changes["change_seq"] > current_seq]
        
        # Sort by change_seq for deterministic order
        changes = changes.sort_values("change_seq").reset_index(drop=True)
        
        # Apply changes in order
        for _, change_row in changes.iterrows():
            change_seq = change_row["change_seq"]
            new_email = change_row["email"]
            new_phone = change_row["phone"]
            new_tier = change_row["tier"]
            
            # Store old values for comparison
            old_email = current_email
            old_phone = current_phone
            old_tier = current_tier
            
            # Apply field rules
            # NULL means leave as is
            # '<<NULL>>' means set to NULL
            # other value means set to value
            
            if not pd.isna(new_email) and new_email != "<<NULL>>":
                current_email = new_email
            elif new_email == "<<NULL>>":
                current_email = np.nan
            # else: new_email is NA, leave as is
            
            if not pd.isna(new_phone) and new_phone != "<<NULL>>":
                current_phone = new_phone
            elif new_phone == "<<NULL>>":
                current_phone = np.nan
            # else: new_phone is NA, leave as is
            
            if not pd.isna(new_tier) and new_tier != "<<NULL>>":
                current_tier = new_tier
            elif new_tier == "<<NULL>>":
                current_tier = np.nan
            # else: new_tier is NA, leave as is
            
            # Check if this is a no-op (NULL-safe comparison)
            # For existing customer: check if any field changed
            if customer_exists:
                email_changed = not (
                    (pd.isna(old_email) and pd.isna(current_email)) or
                    (not pd.isna(old_email) and not pd.isna(current_email) and old_email == current_email)
                )
                phone_changed = not (
                    (pd.isna(old_phone) and pd.isna(current_phone)) or
                    (not pd.isna(old_phone) and not pd.isna(current_phone) and old_phone == current_phone)
                )
                tier_changed = not (
                    (pd.isna(old_tier) and pd.isna(current_tier)) or
                    (not pd.isna(old_tier) and not pd.isna(current_tier) and old_tier == current_tier)
                )
                
                if email_changed or phone_changed or tier_changed:
                    # Not a no-op, advance watermark
                    current_seq = change_seq
            else:
                # Customer creation is never a no-op
                current_seq = change_seq
                customer_exists = True
        
        # Add result row
        result_rows.append({
            "customer_id": cust_id,
            "email": current_email,
            "phone": current_phone,
            "tier": current_tier,
            "updated_seq": current_seq
        })
    
    new_profile = pd.DataFrame(result_rows)
    
    # Ensure proper order and types
    new_profile = new_profile[["customer_id", "email", "phone", "tier", "updated_seq"]]
    new_profile["customer_id"] = new_profile["customer_id"].astype("int64")
    new_profile["updated_seq"] = new_profile["updated_seq"].astype("int64")
    
    return {"new_profile": new_profile}
